text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Shared decision-making: combined psychotherapy and an antidepressant for a recurrent, moderately severe episode; she chose cognitive behavioral therapy and sertraline
  • Start sertraline 50 mg each morning; check tolerability and safety at two weeks; increase to 100 mg if the PHQ-9 has fallen by less than 50 percent after four to six weeks
  • Weekly cognitive behavioral therapy with the clinic psychologist, by video or in person, for about 16 sessions, including behavioral activation and insomnia components
  • Collaborative safety plan with warning signs, coping steps, people to contact, the clinic number, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; medicines stored safely and dispensed in 30-day supplies
  • Psychiatry consultation to confirm the diagnosis, exclude bipolar disorder and PTSD, and advise on treatment of a recurrent episode
  • PHQ-9 at every visit and at least monthly until remission; suicide-risk review at every visit; continue sertraline for at least twelve months after remission because the episode is recurrent
  • Burnout and work: two weeks of medical leave, then a phased return with a 45-hour cap, no field deployment for at least six months, delegation of the families' correspondence, and a peer support group for relief workers
  • Sleep and activity: fixed wake time, no work after 8 pm, a daily 30-minute walk, regular meals, and limited alcohol; prolonged bed rest or withdrawal from activity is explained as unhelpful for depression
  • Screen for bipolar disorder, PTSD, anxiety, and unhealthy alcohol use, and check thyroid, blood count, vitamin B12, and a metabolic panel for medical contributors to fatigue

resource.title: Clara Barton synthetic care plan
resource.description: Treat a recurrent, moderately severe episode of major depressive disorder in a 52-year-old nurse and relief-agency leader after a prolonged wartime deployment, following the 2022 VA/DoD guideline and the CMID depression monograph: shared decision-making for combined psychotherapy and an SSRI, a two-week tolerability and safety check, PHQ-9 at least monthly to response and remission, dose titration for partial response, suicide-risk review with a safety plan and the 988 Lifeline at every visit, sleep, burnout, and a phased return to work, social support, and continuation treatment after remission, while explaining that prolonged rest is not a treatment for depression.
